messages:
sasha: Heads up — ran a few long-context regressions with FP8 dominant profiles and saw headwise drift: certain attention heads flip sign/scale after ~2k tokens, causing factual hallucination spikes. Reproducible on dedicated QA cluster.

liam: Oof. Do you have a minimal repro + config? Could be kv-cache packing or scale overflow.

sasha: Minimal repro command: `python bench_chat.py --model=redwood/llama-3-70b --quant=fp8-mixed --cache-mode=packed --max-tokens=4096 --seed=42`
Config excerpt:
```
quant_profile: fp8-mixed
fallback_policy: int8-on-overflow
kv_cache: packed
per_head_scaling: false
```
Observed: after token ~2100, head 6 and 7 logits magnitude drops by ~8x then some tokens spike. Logs attached (short snippet):
```
[info] token_idx=2098 head=6 pre_attn_mean=0.012 post_attn_mean=0.0012 scale_ratio=0.1
[info] token_idx=2102 head=7 pre_attn_mean=0.02 post_attn_mean=0.16 scale_ratio=8.0
```

jenna: Interesting. Two hypotheses: (A) FP8 dynamic range/exp bias interacting with cached kv rescaling, (B) per-head variance amplification when mixing fp8 and int8 paths. Did you try `per_head_scaling: true`?

sasha: Not yet. Tried forcing fallback to int8 globally for the whole run — drift disappears but latency + cost jump.

kevin: If per-head scaling fixes it, we still need an interface story: runtime currently only accepts a single quant_profile per-layer. We could extend profile metadata to include `headwise_scale` boolean and per-head calibration tensors (small). Tradeoff: more metadata to store/serve, larger profile cache, but might avoid global int8 fallback.

liam: Agree. Also consider a safety-first runtime fallback: detect abrupt per-head scale change > x and locally switch that head to int8 path for next N tokens. That keeps cost localized. But complexity: we need atomicity guarantees when mutating head-level execution kernel.

jenna: Ops implications: storing per-head calibration tensors per model-version increases customer upload and download times. Maybe use delta-encoding for per-head scales (store base + sparse deltas). Also need eval metrics: A/B test headwise vs layerwise to quantify quality gain per token.

sasha: My quick local patch toggling `per_head_scaling=true` fixed the immediate drift on QA. I'll run full sweep across seeds and contexts.

kevin: For API/contract: propose adding to quant_profile model metadata keys: `headwise_scale: true|false`, `head_scale_blob_id: <blob>` (optional), `fallback_granularity: head|layer|model`. Keep defaults conservative (false, layer, none).

liam: Implementation notes: runtime must be able to hot-swap kernel for single attention head without full model relaunch. That's feasible if we treat attention as per-head microkernels with indirection table. Perf cost? small if we cache kernel combos.

jenna: Also add telemetry: per-head variance, sudden scale_ratio > 4 events, and head-fallbacks initiated. Tie to alerts when head-fallback > threshold for multiple customers.

sasha: Action items:
- I will run comprehensive repro with `per_head_scaling=true` and attach diffs (sasha) — due EOD tomorrow.
- kevin: draft quant_profile metadata proposal and perf implications doc (this week).
- liam: prototype runtime indirection for per-head kernel hot-swap and microbench (next sprint).
- jenna: design telemetry buckets and alert thresholds (this week).

runtime-bot: Canary test started for `sasha/repro/fp8-drift` on qa-cluster-2 (run id r-2024-07-21-09). Logs will be posted here. :robot_face:

kevin: One more design question — do we require model owners to ship per-head calibration, or can we fallback to on-device quick calibrate (cheap single-pass stats) at load time? On-device might be good but adds startup latency per container. Thoughts?

liam: Prefer optional upload with runtime quick-calibrate fallback. Default: if `head_scale_blob_id` missing, runtime runs a 1-epoch quick stat pass on a small heldout to compute head scales (configurable window). Document cost and SLO for that.

jenna: SGTM. Let's keep the default conservative to avoid silent quality regression. Document in the profile schema that missing blobs imply runtime quick-calibrate and possible initial slowdown.

sasha: Thanks team — will share results tomorrow. If `per_head_scaling` looks stable we can avoid a full int8 fallback policy and reduce customer cost impact. :crossed_fingers:
